faq.title: Pricing questions
faq.subtitle: The billing details people ask about most. Setup, the AI, integrations and security are covered on the full FAQ.

items.q: What do the plans cost?
items.a: Free is $0. Monthly plans are Starter at $12 with $7 of AI credit each month, Growth at $59 with $40, and Scale at $299 with $240. Annual billing is about two months free — you pay for roughly ten months and get twelve: Starter is $120 a year ($10/month), Growth is $588 ($49/month), and Scale is $2,988 ($249/month).

items.q: How does the AI allowance work?
items.a: Free includes 100 AI messages a month. Each reply the AI sends counts as one message, so a short chat uses a few and a long back-and-forth uses more. Paid plans work differently: they include a monthly AI credit that the AI spends as it works, so a quick question uses less than a long back-and-forth. Starter includes $7 of credit a month, Growth $40 and Scale $240.

items.q: Do escalations cost anything?
items.a: No extra charge. The handoff itself is free on every plan, and the AI stops the moment a person takes over. On Free, messages the AI already sent before the handoff still count toward your 100; on paid plans, the AI only spends credit while it is answering, and the AI stops spending credit the moment a person takes over.

items.q: Can the AI issue refunds?
items.a: Only if the workspace owner turns refunds on. They're off by default. Even with refunds off, the AI can look up the payment and offer to connect the customer with your team.

items.q: What happens when I use up my AI allowance?
items.a: The AI hands new conversations straight to your team instead of answering. On a paid plan you can top up credit at any time, or turn on automatic recharge so it never stops. Top-ups never expire. Your monthly credit resets each billing period.

items.q: Do I pay for each teammate?
items.a: No. Seats are unlimited on every plan, including Free, so adding a teammate costs nothing. Seats and AI credit are billed completely separately — adding a teammate never touches your AI allowance.

items.q: Can I cancel anytime?
items.a: Yes, from Settings → Billing, no lock-in. Cancellation takes effect at the end of the current billing period, so you keep what you paid for until then.

items.q: What happens if I stop paying?
items.a: The workspace drops to the Free plan at the end of the period. Your knowledge base, conversation history, and settings all stay intact.

items: What is MCP?
The Model Context Protocol, a standard way for an AI to call tools on another system. Connect an MCP server and Elpino discovers its tools. You then choose which ones the agent may use.
How many MCP servers can I connect?
Up to five, with up to 15 tools enabled per server.
Can the agent change things in my systems?
Only through tools you've switched on, and tools that change data always require a customer whose email has been verified.
How does it know who the customer is?
From the conversation, earlier chats with them, and a verification step: a one-time email code or a signed token from your app.
Can it issue refunds?
Only if the workspace owner turns refunds on. They're off by default.
What happens when it can't solve something?
It says so and asks the customer whether to connect them with your team. Everyone on the team gets a Join alert for 90 seconds, and if nobody joins a ticket is created automatically.

chaptersSection.label: The chapters
chaptersSection.subtitle: Each control names the part of the system it lives in and the guarantee it gives you — not the exact mechanism behind it.

accounts.title: Accounts & sessions
accounts.kicker: Who is on your team, and how we know it's them.
accounts.intro: Sign-up, sign-in and every session after it. Passwords are never kept in a readable form, verification codes expire quickly, and a session can be ended from the server at any time.

1.1.title: Passwords are hashed, never stored
1.1.text: Your password is never kept anywhere in a form anyone could read back — not even us. Checking it can't leak how close a wrong guess was.

1.2.title: Email verification codes
1.2.text: New accounts confirm their address with a short-lived code. Only a secure hash of it is stored, it expires quickly, and only a few wrong attempts are allowed before you need a fresh one.

1.3.title: Google sign-in is checked on the server
1.3.text: The Google sign-in popup runs in your browser, but our server independently verifies it before trusting it, and always signs you into the same account by your verified email — never a second, unlinked one.

1.4.title: Signed session tokens
1.4.text: Your session is a signed token our server can always verify on its own — it can't be forged, edited or replayed as something it isn't.

1.5.title: A locked-down session cookie
1.5.text: Your session cookie can't be read by page scripts, and only ever travels over a secure connection.

1.6.title: Sign out everywhere
1.6.text: Signing out invalidates every one of your sessions quickly. If we can't confirm a session is still valid, it's refused rather than let through.

1.7.title: Safe redirects
1.7.text: After signing in, you're only ever sent to a page on our own site — never somewhere else, no matter how the link is crafted.

1.8.title: Team invitations
1.8.text: Invitation links are unguessable and expire automatically, and an owner decides whether members can invite others at all.

front-door.title: The front door
front-door.kicker: What the website does before a request goes any further.
front-door.intro: The web app is the first thing a browser touches. It hardens the browser, limits abuse, and validates input before anything is passed on.

2.1.title: Browser hardening headers
2.1.text: Every page except the chat widget is protected against clickjacking, guarded against content-type sniffing, and has sensitive device permissions like camera and location switched off by default. The widget is the one deliberate exception, since it has to live inside an iframe on your site.

2.2.title: Shared abuse limits
2.2.text: Public forms are protected by rate limits shared across every server we run, so abuse from one place can't slip through by simply hitting a different one.

2.3.title: It fails closed
2.3.text: If the abuse limiter can't be reached, the request is refused rather than waved through.

2.4.title: Validated, length-capped input
2.4.text: Every form is checked and size-limited on the server before anything is processed — never trusted just because the browser already validated it.

gateway.title: The gateway
gateway.kicker: One door for the backend, closed by default.
gateway.intro: Every call to the backend goes through a single gateway. The rule is simple: if a route isn't explicitly public, it needs to prove it belongs.

3.1.title: Closed by default
3.1.text: Every route requires proof it's an authorized internal call, unless it's explicitly marked public. If that check isn't configured, the gateway refuses everything rather than failing open.

3.2.title: A short, explicit public list
3.2.text: Only callers that genuinely can't hold internal credentials are public: the chat widget, page analytics, the payment webhook, and one-time secure links. Each one is marked deliberately, route by route.

3.3.title: Explicit origins only
3.3.text: The API answers browsers only from a known, approved list of origins — never from anywhere that happens to ask.

3.4.title: Verified live connections
3.4.text: Live-view connections require a verified, workspace-scoped credential with an expiry. Anything else is dropped immediately.

3.5.title: Internal pushes are guarded too
3.5.text: The endpoints services use to push live notifications to dashboards require the same internal proof, so nobody outside can ring a teammate's screen.

visitors.title: Visitors & identity
visitors.kicker: Telling a logged-in customer from someone who just typed an email.
visitors.intro: A name, an email or an order number is not proof of who someone is. Account help unlocks only after real proof of identity, and that proof expires quickly.

4.1.title: Guests stay guests
4.1.text: A typed name, email, phone or payment reference never counts as proof of identity. Guests can chat and leave contact details, but that unlocks no private tools and is never merged into anyone else's history.

4.2.title: Signed identity from your own site
4.2.text: For logged-in customers, your own server vouches for who they are with a short-lived signed credential that only you and Elpino can create together. Contact details only count as verified when your system says they are.

4.3.title: One exchange, one session
4.3.text: Each proof of identity is used once, then exchanged for a fresh session of its own — nothing reusable is kept lying around, and what is stored can't be turned back into the original.

4.4.title: Short-lived sessions
4.4.text: A session expires automatically after a period of inactivity, or a fixed time from sign-in — whichever comes first. It's held only in the widget's own memory, never in browser storage or a URL.

4.5.title: Rotation and logout
4.5.text: Rotating your identity credential invalidates every session that used the old one immediately. Logging out revokes the session on our server, and old sessions are cleaned up automatically.

4.6.title: Email codes for guests
4.6.text: A visitor can also verify by email with a short one-time code, rate-limited to prevent abuse. Verifying only unlocks that one conversation, and only for a limited time.

4.7.title: Every request is re-checked
4.7.text: Every authenticated read and write independently re-checks who's asking, what workspace it's scoped to, and whether that access is still valid — nothing is trusted just because it was valid a moment ago.

ai.title: The AI's leash
ai.kicker: What the AI can and can't do, enforced by the backend, not by asking nicely.
ai.intro: The model proposes; the backend decides. Tools, identity, limits and money all live outside the model, where a clever message can't talk its way past them.

5.1.title: One reply, one owner
5.1.text: Before an AI reply is saved, the system independently confirms the conversation is still AI-owned and the question being answered is still the latest one. The AI can't talk over your team or answer something that's already moved on.

5.2.title: Bounded work
5.2.text: Every AI turn has a hard ceiling on how much it can do. A stuck or looping run is cut off automatically, never left running.

5.3.title: The backend chooses the tools
5.3.text: Which tools the AI can use is decided entirely by your workspace's own setup and the customer's verification — the model can't grant itself a tool, declare data public, or reach into another workspace.

5.4.title: Account tools need a verified customer
5.4.text: Payment lookups and connected systems only become available once the customer has proved who they are, and only ever act on the identity already on file — never on whatever the model is told.

5.5.title: Messages are data, not instructions
5.5.text: Customer messages, documents and tool results reach the model clearly labeled as untrusted information. Instructions hidden inside them are not followed.

5.6.title: A second opinion
5.6.text: A separate, independent check reviews each draft reply against the evidence the AI actually gathered. An unsupported claim is sent back for a rewrite, and one that still fails gets handed to a person.

5.7.title: Money moves behind gates
5.7.text: AI refunds are off until a workspace owner turns them on, and even then are limited and capped automatically. A retried refund can never be issued twice, and cancelling a subscription never cuts off time you've already paid for.

5.8.title: An audit trail for every run
5.8.text: Every AI run keeps a record of what it did and what it used to do it. Anything that touches money is also logged as a note your team can see.

private-data.title: Private data
private-data.intro: Before any request reaches an AI model, identifying details are replaced with safe placeholders. Try it below with your own text.

6.1.title: Real details never reach the model
6.1.text: Names, emails, phone numbers, addresses and order or payment details are never sent to the AI model as-is. We swap them for safe placeholders first, and only restore the real value afterward, on our own servers — never inside anything the model sees.

6.2.title: Secrets are removed, not just hidden
6.2.text: Passwords, API keys, tokens and one-time codes are stripped out entirely before anything reaches a model — not disguised, just gone.

6.3.title: Sensitive links are cleaned
6.3.text: Links carrying access tokens or other sensitive parameters are cleaned before a model ever reads them.

6.4.title: Payment facts, not payment records
6.4.text: Payment tools only ever return safe summaries — status and dates — never raw card or account details, and failure reasons are simplified rather than passed through as free text.

6.5.title: The same rules for every model
6.5.text: The same protection runs no matter which AI provider answers, including when we fall back to another one. Your conversations and documents are never used to train general-purpose models.

integrations.title: Integrations & outbound requests
integrations.kicker: When Elpino has to reach out to a URL you gave us.
integrations.intro: Crawling your site, reading a page, or calling a connected system all mean fetching a URL a person typed in. Each of those requests is locked down so it can't be turned against our own network — or yours.

7.1.title: Credentials are encrypted at rest
7.1.text: Any key or token you connect — Stripe, Razorpay, Trello and the like — is encrypted before it's ever stored. A database copy alone can't recover them.

7.2.title: Outbound requests can't be aimed inward
7.2.text: When we fetch a URL on your behalf — crawling your site, calling a connected system — we make sure it can't be redirected at a private network or internal infrastructure instead, including ours.

7.3.title: Redirects are checked every step
7.3.text: We follow redirects carefully, checking each hop rather than trusting the final destination, and only ever over standard, secure connections.

7.4.title: Connected systems are limited
7.4.text: Connections to your own tools are capped in size and time, so they can't be used to pull unbounded data or hang indefinitely.

7.5.title: Admins approve every tool
7.5.text: Connected tools are off until an admin approves them. A tool that can change data is flagged separately, and still needs a verified customer even when the server itself is otherwise public.

7.6.title: Disconnect means gone
7.6.text: When you disconnect an integration, its stored tokens and credentials are wiped immediately.

secure-links.title: Secure handovers
secure-links.kicker: When a customer has to send something sensitive.
secure-links.intro: Never paste a key into a chat. A teammate can ask for it through a one-time link instead, and the chat only ever holds the link.

8.1.title: The chat never holds the secret
8.1.text: The notice in the conversation names what was asked for and carries a link — never the value itself.

8.2.title: An unguessable, short-lived link
8.2.text: The link itself is the customer's entire proof of authorization, so it's made unguessable, and it expires automatically before it can become a standing risk.

8.3.title: Encrypted with its own key
8.3.text: Whatever's submitted is sealed using a key kept entirely separate from the one that protects your other credentials, so either can be rotated — or, worst case, exposed — without touching the other.

8.4.title: Capped and swept
8.4.text: Submissions are size-limited, and anything expired is automatically and permanently wiped on a regular schedule, leaving only a record that something happened — never what it was.

money.title: Money & billing
money.kicker: Payments, renewals and the limits tied to them.
money.intro: Anything that moves money is verified twice: once that the message really came from the payment provider, and once that it can't be applied twice.

9.1.title: Signed webhooks and checkouts
9.1.text: Payment notifications are only accepted with a valid, verified signature from the provider — anything else, including a near-miss, is rejected outright.

9.2.title: Replays can't reset usage
9.2.text: A payment notification that arrives more than once — replayed, or simply delivered twice — can never re-zero already-spent usage or re-grant credit.

9.3.title: Auto-recharge can't double-charge
9.3.text: Checking that a recharge is within its limit and actually reserving it happen as one atomic step, and your balance is only ever credited once a payment is confirmed and captured.

9.4.title: Every money movement is on record
9.4.text: Every payment event from the provider is written to an audit trail, and any payment action the AI takes gets its own separate log.

9.5.title: Plan limits are enforced on the server
9.5.text: Plan-gated features are checked in the backend, not just hidden in the interface, and seat limits are counted from real membership — not from what the browser claims.

lifecycle.title: Data lifecycle
lifecycle.kicker: Where data lives, how long, and how it goes away.
lifecycle.intro: Your data is scoped to your workspace, expires when it should, and can be removed by you.

10.1.title: Scoped to your workspace
10.1.text: Conversations, knowledge, customers and settings all belong to a workspace, and every lookup is scoped to it — nothing crosses over by accident.

10.2.title: Team-only stays team-only
10.2.text: Notes marked team-only are filtered out before a conversation is ever shown to the visitor's widget.

10.3.title: Short-lived things expire
10.3.text: Verification codes, session credentials and secure-link content are all automatically expired and cleaned up — nothing short-lived is kept around indefinitely.

10.4.title: Delete your workspace
10.4.text: Deleting a workspace cancels its subscription immediately and removes its records, with a firm outer limit set in the privacy policy for full removal.

10.5.title: Leave or delete your account
10.5.text: People can leave a workspace, and an account can be deleted entirely from Settings.

infrastructure.title: Infrastructure
infrastructure.kicker: How the services themselves are run.
infrastructure.intro: Plain, unglamorous hygiene that keeps an internal service from becoming a public one.

11.1.title: Internal services aren't publicly reachable
11.1.text: Our backend services and database aren't exposed to the public internet at all — only a single, hardened entry point is.

11.2.title: Lean production builds
11.2.text: What actually runs in production carries nothing extra — no development tools, no unused dependencies.

11.3.title: Limits, health checks and log rotation
11.3.text: Every service runs with resource limits, automatic health checks and a restart policy, and logs are rotated so they can't grow unbounded.

11.4.title: Secrets stay out of source
11.4.text: Keys and secrets are never checked into our codebase — they're supplied to each service separately, and sensitive credential files are mounted read-only.

11.5.title: Repeatable deploys
11.5.text: Every deployment goes through the same automated checks, so a release is never a one-off manual process.

verification.title: How we check our own work
verification.kicker: The tests that try to break the rules above.
verification.intro: Security claims are only worth what tests back them. These are covered by automated tests in our own codebase.

12.1.title: Identity regressions
12.1.text: Automated tests cover forged credentials, expired and replayed sessions, logout, credential rotation, and that one workspace can never see another's data.

12.2.title: Outbound request tests
12.2.text: The checks that stop outbound requests from reaching internal networks have their own dedicated tests.

12.3.title: Privacy filter tests
12.3.text: The system that replaces private details before they reach a model, and the payment-facts rules that limit what it can be shown, are both directly tested.

12.4.title: Billing correctness tests
12.4.text: Renewal replays and signature verification are covered by tests, so a billing fix can't quietly reopen a hole that was already closed.

items.q: How is this different from a generic chatbot widget?
items.a: Elpino answers only from the knowledge you gave it, can look up real payments and use your own tools, verifies identity before touching anything personal, and hands over to a person with the full conversation when it can't help.

items.q: How fast can I set it up on my own?

items.q: How does it decide between answering and alerting me?
items.a: If it can answer from your knowledge or a tool, it does. If it can't, it says so and asks the customer whether to connect them with your team. Only then are you and your team alerted.

items.q: Will it make things up?
items.a: It answers from what you've approved, and a review pass checks drafts against tool results. When it doesn't know, it says so.

items.q: Is my Stripe or Razorpay account safe?
items.a: Credentials are stored encrypted, and money-moving actions such as refunds are off unless you turn them on.

items.q: What happens when I hire a support person?
items.a: Invite them and they'll get Join alerts, can take over chats from the AI, and can hand them back.

items.q: Do I have to use identity verification?
items.a: No, but it's what lets the AI safely show private data. Anyone can type any email into a chat, so a signed token from your own login system is how a customer becomes Verified.

items.q: How long does a token last?
items.a: At most five minutes, and it works once. The chat session itself lasts up to 8 hours, with a 30-minute idle limit.

items.q: Which signing algorithm?
items.a: HS256. Other algorithms, including none and RS256, are refused.

items.q: Which languages have snippets?
items.a: Node.js, Python, PHP and Ruby, in your dashboard's identity settings and the docs.

items.q: What is an MCP server?
items.a: A service that exposes tools over the Model Context Protocol. Elpino discovers its tools, and you enable the ones the AI may use.

items.q: Can the AI change data in my systems?
items.a: Only through tools you've enabled, and tools that change data always need a verified customer.

items.q: Is there an API?
items.a: The widget SDK, identity tokens and MCP are the integration surface today.
